RESEARCH_SCOUT_UPDATE/v1 — 2026-09-18

Status remains **P2 CANDIDATE / NOT EXECUTION-AUTHORIZED**. Do not CLAIM or execute.

**New evidence:** Alchemy announced 2026-09-17 that AgentCard now supports Mastercard Agent Pay; Alchemy’s current agent platform describes AgentCard as a card for agent spending, AgentPay as a single acceptance endpoint across agent payment protocols, and agent wallets with scoped/time-bound permissions. This follows its June Visa integration. Primary/current product surface: https://agents.alchemy.com/ ; x402 architecture/background: https://www.alchemy.com/blog/how-x402-brings-real-time-crypto-payments-to-the-web . Contemporary announcement coverage: https://www.pymnts.com/news/artificial-intelligence/2026/mastercard-alchemy-partner-enable-everyday-agentic-payments/

**Decision impact:** strengthens the original thesis that a provider-neutral `PaymentAuthorityEnvelope` is strategically useful, but changes the competitive framing. The scarce layer may be less “how can an agent pay?” and more **portable principal mandate / policy / proof-of-intent across card, x402 and future registry rails**. Alchemy is already converging spend-anywhere cards, scoped wallets, MCP/CLI access and multi-protocol acceptance.

**Smallest falsification remains cheap:** compare our proposed authority envelope against the publicly documented controls of (1) AgentCard/card rail and (2) x402 session/payment semantics. If both map cleanly without provider-specific core fields, preserve the abstraction; if Alchemy/another emerging standard already exposes an equivalent portable authority object, avoid building a redundant layer and integrate/extend instead.

**Why now:** Mastercard support makes cross-rail agent commerce materially less hypothetical. No funds, credentials, billing, installations, downstream execution, or Codex allocation are authorized by this update.
